evidence.note: Front-loads vendored-lib download + SHA256 verification (fatal gate) and foundations (config, database) first, then lays out an architecture ordering storage → models → auth → seed → main routes → templates → static → start.sh: a defensible dependency-aware build order.

Rolling per-step 'Plan:' enumerates remaining subsystems (accounts, statuses, timelines, notifications, search, lists, admin, media, polls) in a foundations-then-features order, but as a flat re-stated feature list rather than a maintained milestone hierarchy with per-item done-checks.
Done-checks are generic (py_compile, 'import OK', smoke test) rather than milestone-specific acceptance criteria defined up front; verification is mostly 'does it compile/respond'.
Contract-specific verification (OAuth token issuance, CSP header, cookie HttpOnly/SameSite) appears only in a late testing phase — emergent, not pre-declared as milestone gates.

A long JOIN-column-collision debugging spiral dominated the back half; the milestone plan did not sequence to retire highest-risk items and the agent submitted with acknowledged unresolved bugs (wrong account.id, CSP unsafe-inline), showing milestones were aspirational lists not driving de-risking.

reasoning: The agent used a sensible, dependency-aware build order — fatal hash gate and durable storage/auth before endpoints, vendored libs before UI — which exceeds a flat unordered list (anchor 3) and matches the 'sensible ordered plan, foundations before features, rough done-criteria' description of anchor 5, edged toward 6 by deliberately front-loading the SHA256 gate. It falls short of anchor 8 because the milestones are a rolling per-step feature list rather than a maintained hierarchy, done-criteria are generic (compile/import/smoke) rather than explicit per-milestone verification hooks defined up front, and the sequencing did not drive de-risking of the highest-value subsystems (it stalled in a JOIN-bug spiral and shipped with known defects).
